name: How can I add under-cabinet lighting without seeing wires everywhere?

mainEntity.name: How can I add under-cabinet lighting without seeing wires everywhere?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Under-cabinet lighting is most useful when it illuminates the countertop rather than the cabinet doors or the person standing at the counter. A continuous, well-diffused system usually gives more even task light than widely spaced bright points.

**Context:** Kitchen lighting must be coordinated with cabinet construction, backsplash materials, outlets, and countertop work areas. Surface-mounted channels, recessed systems, and integrated fixtures each have different installation and repair implications.

**Key factors:**
- Cabinet depth and underside clearance
- Countertop color and reflectivity
- Switch location and dimming needs
- Cable access before cabinets and backsplash are installed

**Practical guidance:** Decide whether the system should be controlled with the general kitchen lights or separately. Finalize wiring and fixture locations before cabinets, tile, or backsplash work begins.

Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate under-cabinet lighting with kitchen layout, cabinetry, and finish installation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Plan the wiring before cabinets and backsplash materials are installed, then place the light toward the front of the cabinet underside so it illuminates the counter. Use diffused fixtures and a separate, accessible control when possible. Cabinet depth, outlets, and backsplash details affect the cleanest installation method.
